What Percent of Libertarians Vote for the Libertarian Party?

I personally believe that by voting you are granting legitimacy to the political process and on an individual level you are attempting to exert your beliefs on others through force. I don't want the US government to force everyone to have libertarian ideals, I just don't want them to interfere with mine. If the libertarian party ran on a platform of strictly REPEALING laws with no additional laws put in their place then maybe I would change my tune. All too often you wind up with situations like "free trade acts" which have thousands of pages detailing how exactly to make free trade instead of simply repealing tariffs, taxes, and fees.

I believe in libertarianism, but I'm not a part of nor vote for the LP. It's simply a matter of practicality and pragmatism on two important fronts.

Front 1) Voting for the LP is the same as throwing away my vote. The LP doesn't have a snowball's chance in hell of even achieving enough votes to get attention on the news, much less become powerful enough to have a say in US politics. If I want to exercise one of the few freedoms I have, I'm going to do it smartly in a way that advances my own interests--something that I think all other libertarians would agree is part of being libertarian.

Front 2) I believe in the ideals of libertarianism, and I think the US would be a better stronger nation if it embraced more of those ideals. However (and this is speaking as someone with degrees in political science as well as international relations, plus professional experience), I seriously doubt that the US could successfully implement such changes in a way that doesn't cause more problems than it solves.

Also I'm a bit of a black sheep. One of my specialties is climate security, particularly how climate change affects the US military, creates security threats abroad, and threatens US infrastructure. Climate security is a collective action problem, but virtually no libertarian candidate or organization acknowledges it as an issue.

I vote Libertarian as much as I am able.

In my state, almost all of the real local elections are decided in the R or D primary, depending on which part of the state you live in. The L party only has guaranteed ballot access for the state wide offices without a complicated and onerous petition drive. Statewide Libertarian Party candidates are selected at a convention, and we have open primaries, so there is nothing stopping any voter from voting in either primary - which I do.

Plus, election winners have to have 50% plus one of the votes, so sometimes we have a runoff.
Just wondering, In your state what percentage does a 3rd party need to get in a election to get major party status?

If it is a duly blessed and recognized political party, 1% of registered voters in the previous election.

For other races, we need petitions signed by 5% of registered voters in the district - but the appointed judge can wait until just before the election and throw out any or all of the petitions without allowing time enough for an appeal.
That 1% would be nice. In 2014 the Libertarian Party in my state polled at over 4 and a half percent and still didn't get status.

Turkey Casserole

An old twitter friend sent me this recipe and let me tell you, it tastes good. it is low carb, my bg stayed level after only a 20 point raise. The casserole tasted like Turkey with stuffing mixed in, I really enjoyed how tender the ground turkey was. The really cool thing is, I didn't think this casserole was going to get thick enough to be a true casserole but it did!

Ingredients

  • 2 cup chicken broth, low sodium
  • 1 cup fresh chopped celery
  • 1/2 cup fresh chopped onion
  • 1 cup frozen green peas, thawed
  • 1 1/2 cup plain croutons, dry
  • 1 1/2 skinless cooked turkey breast, diced
  • 1 tsp parsley, dried
  • 1 tsp sage, ground
  • 1/8 tsp black pepper
  • 1 Soup, chicken, creamy, canned, Microwaved

Directions

  • 1 Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
  • 2 Mix together 1 cup chicken broth, celery, and onion in a large saucepan and cook over medium heat until veggies are tender. Add diced turkey breast. Add peas, bread cubes, parsley flakes, poultry seasoning, and black pepper.
  • 3 In a bowl, mix together the remaining 1 cup of chicken broth and cream of chicken soup. Add this to the other ingredients.
  • 4 Spoon mixture into an 8-by-8-inch baking dish sprayed with butter-flavored cooking spray and bake for 45 to 50 minutes.
  • 5 Remove from oven and let sit for 5 minutes before dividing and serving.
